title: Urban company
author: VIKAS KUMAR
body:
Urban Company Placement Experience: Category Manager (On-Campus)

Name: Vikas Kumar

Branch: Industrial and Production Engineering

Role: Category Manager

Mode: On-campus

Round 1: Online Assessment

The first round was an online assessment made up of basic aptitude questions. It was not very difficult, but accuracy and time management mattered because shortlisting depended on it.

Shortlisting for Interviews

After the assessment, the company shared a list of shortlisted students for the interviews. The interviews were conducted based on priority: Priority 0, Priority 1 and then Priority 2. Priority 0 students were given the most preference. If the company found the number of candidates it was looking for in Priority 0, it did not move on to Priority 1, and similarly for Priority 2. So it is important to perform well in the assessment to land in a higher priority group.

Round 2: First Interview (about 30 minutes)

My first interview lasted about 30 minutes and focused mainly on my positions of responsibility during college. The interviewer asked me about my roles and about anything crazy or challenging I had done, and he went deep into my internship experience. He was looking for candidates with great communication skills who had actually taken up responsibilities and ownership.

My fellow students told me that in their interviews they were also asked to solve guesstimates, Excel questions and a few numerical problems. Questions about the company and its products also came up. One question that was common in every interview was: Why should we hire you?

Round 3: Second Interview

After the first interview, students were shortlisted again for the second round. This round also focused mainly on my positions of responsibility, along with these topics:

- What I know about the company

- Whether I fit the Category Manager role and why

- The impact I have created in my previous roles and experiences

Tips for Juniors

1. Know your resume inside out. Every responsibility and internship you mention can be questioned in depth.

2. Be ready to talk about impact, not just duties. Explain what changed because of your work, ideally with numbers.

3. Research Urban Company well: its services, business model, and what a Category Manager does there.

4. Prepare a strong, personalized answer to "Why should we hire you?"

5. Brush up on basic aptitude, Excel and puzzles, since they can be asked.

6. Communication matters a lot, so speak clearly and structure your answers.

While answering, use the STAR technique: explain the Situation, the Task you were responsible for, the Action you took, and the Result you achieved. It keeps your answers structured and shows your impact clearly.

I wish you all the best my friends. Just be confident and I know you will rock it.

title: Urban Company
author: PRITAM ANAND
body:
By: Pritam Anand
Date: 17 October 2026

Role: Category Manager

1. What Urban Company Looks For

Urban Company values ownership, structured problem-solving, confidence, and a strong sense of responsibility. Beyond technical knowledge, the interview focuses on how you approach real-world problems, make decisions, and take responsibility for outcomes.

Analytical Thinking: Demonstrate your ability to break down problems, analyze data, and develop practical solutions.
Ownership & Leadership: Highlight situations where you took initiative, coordinated teams, and managed responsibilities.
Role Alignment: Connect your academic projects, internships, and extracurricular activities with the responsibilities of a Category Manager.
2. How to Present Your Experience

While discussing internships, projects, and positions of responsibility, focus on the problems you addressed, the decisions you made, and the value you created.

Internships: Explain the problem you worked on, your approach, and the solution you proposed.
Projects: Be clear about the objective, methodology, and practical application of your work.
Leadership: Use examples from club activities and event management to demonstrate teamwork, planning, coordination, and problem-solving.

Don't just describe what you did. Explain why you did it, how you handled challenges, and what you would improve if given another opportunity.

3. Key Lessons from the Interview
Be clear and confident about why you want to join Urban Company.
Never present the role as an experiment or merely an opportunity to gain experience. Demonstrate genuine commitment to the responsibilities.
Prepare your resume thoroughly. Be ready to answer follow-up questions about every project, internship, and leadership experience.
Keep your answers structured, relevant, and supported by real examples.
4. Preparation Tips for Future Candidates
Understand the Role: Study the Category Manager job description and prepare for questions related to operations, supply and demand, business metrics, and problem-solving.
Prepare Your Experiences: Develop clear interview stories around your internships, projects, and leadership roles, focusing on your individual contribution.
Practice Guesstimates: Work on estimation problems and learn to break complex questions into logical, manageable steps.
Focus on Business Impact: Explain how your decisions can improve efficiency, service quality, customer experience, or business performance.
Be Yourself: Communicate naturally, listen carefully, and support your answers with genuine examples rather than memorized responses.
Final Words for Juniors

My biggest takeaway is that an interview is not just about what you know, but how you think, communicate, and take ownership. Prepare your experiences well, understand the role, and approach every question with a structured mindset.

Stay confident, be authentic, and focus on the value you can bring to the organization.

All the best to everyone preparing for placements!

title: Urban Company
author: APARNA AGARWAL
body:
I got placed for an operations role. Category Manager at UrbanCompany.

I appeared for 2 more companies before that: Nestle - GET role

Campus Activewear - Production

Resume/Experience/Projects:

I was mainly preparing for Managerial roles. But most common important thing for interviews of all roles, especially for On-Campus companies, is RESUME. Many companies ask ONLY from resumes. EXPERIENCE and PROJECTS are the most important sections.

Operations/Managerial:

I put my clubs' and society's events that i organized as projects. Dashboards and case studies are also often considered relevant projects for such roles.

For experience, i used my two summer internships in anyway i could: highlighting what the company JD/PPT emphasized on.

I was asked my project and experience in-depth in interview for Campus Activewear and UrbanCompany.

GET/Core:

Nestle was for GET role. They had offline objective written test. Then GD and then technical+HR interview round.

Technical was simple electrical concepts and knowledge questions only.

In HR round, they asked questions like:

-a situation where you had conflict with a team member or pointed out their mistake and what was their reaction

-a extremely hard moment in life and how did you overcome it (asked in both Nestle and UrbanCompany)

Communication/ GD:

I had to clear GD in both Campus activeeear and nestle and communication and confidence while speaking is must. Even in interview of course, you should be able to talk!! And talk well.

🛑In interviews, knowing a answer and being able to recall it at the moment is bit difficult. You need to prepare really well to be able to answer the best you can in technical questions. In Campus Activewear, I couldn't answer some questions as well as I could have just because those points didn't click to me at the moment.

title: Urban Company - GURANSH SINGH | Placement Experience
author: GURANSH SINGH
body:
1. What Urban Company Looks For

Urban Company prioritizes mindset, ownership, and clarity over pure domain expertise. Domain-specific technical knowledge alone won't get you through-what matters most is:

Confidence & Preparation: How clearly you communicate your thoughts and how thoroughly you understand your own journey.

Role Alignment: Your fit for the Category Management role based on problem-solving, operational drive, and leadership.

Authenticity: Having well-formed perspectives on the products you've built, the teams you’ve worked with, and the decisions you’ve made in the past.

2. Navigating Past Experience & Impact

When discussing your past internships, projects, or leadership roles, focus heavily on the "Why" and the "Impact":

Understand the Organization: Know exactly what the organization does, what specific role you played, and what measurable impact your work created.

Reflect & Have a Perspective: Be prepared to articulate how you felt about your work, what worked well, what didn't, and how you collaborated with your teams. Urban Company values candidates who genuinely reflect on their experiences rather than just listing bullet points on a resume.

3. The "Never Say" Golden Rule for Candidates

** Do not tell the interviewer that you want to "try out" a role or that you are just looking for "experience."**

If a company offers you an internship or a full-time role, they are investing resources in you. Saying you want to "experiment" or "see if it works" leaves a very poor impression.

Be 100% committed and clear about why you want to be there.

Show total conviction that you are ready to give your 100% to the responsibilities assigned to you.

4. Key Tips for the Interview

Master the Job Description (JD): Thoroughly study the Category Manager JD. Understand the operational metrics, supply-demand dynamics, service quality standards, and growth levers relevant to the role.

Make Yourself Memorable: Don't sound like just another student going through a standard placement routine. Speak with conviction, engage warmly with the managers, and leave a distinct, positive impression.

Maintain High Energy & Professionalism: Speak clearly, build a genuine connection with the interviewing panel, and communicate with structured logic.

Final Words for Junior Batches

If you prepare your past experiences thoroughly, demonstrate high ownership, master the JD, and project absolute confidence, you will crack it.

All the best to my juniors at NIT Jalandhar! May God’s grace be with you all. Hope to see NITJ achieve greater heights in the coming placement seasons!

author: AYUSH AWASTHI
body:
Urban Company

My Interview Experience with Urban Company | Category Manager – Business Operations

I’m happy to share that I have been selected for the Category Manager – Business Operations role at Urban Company!

The interview process was a great learning experience. It helped me understand the importance of structured thinking, practical problem-solving, analytical reasoning, and making decisions in real-world business situations.

For anyone preparing for similar roles, here are a few tips that I believe can make a difference:

Understand the company: Learn about its business model, target customers, services, and revenue streams.

Think practically: Practise real-life business scenarios rather than relying only on theoretical knowledge.

Structure your answers: Break problems into smaller parts, identify the root cause, and explain your solution step by step.

Focus on data and metrics: Understand how numbers can help evaluate business performance and make better decisions.

Be clear with your reasoning: Interviewers want to understand how you approach a problem, not just your final answer.

Show ownership: Demonstrate that you can take responsibility, adapt to challenges, and focus on results.

Stay calm and curious: If you don't know something, be honest and explain how you would approach it.

My biggest takeaway: A good answer matters, but a clear, logical approach to solving a problem matters just as much.

Grateful for this opportunity and excited for the journey ahead!
